mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) as a continuous variable is associated with higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce the discount rate for equity cash flows and increase the attractiveness of equities relative to fixed income.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points over the past 3 months signals a deteriorating labor market, which reduces corporate earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE rise >0.3pp in 3 months), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 0.5% over the past 3 months and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains below 0.5%, it signals a potential for central bank tightening, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 3 months and FEDFUNDS < 0.5%
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises >0.5% in 3 months and FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by HOUST > 1300 and RSAFS > 450000), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a potential supply shock that reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1300 and RSAFS > 450000 and INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher residential investment (RSAFS) as a continuous variable is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as strong housing activity signals robust consumer demand and economic growth, which supports corporate earnings and equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS > 450000, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1300 units in the past month signals a weakening housing market, which reduces consumer confidence and economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls below 1300 in last month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (HOUST < 1300), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When both housing starts (HOUST) and residential investment (RSAFS) decline by more than 1% over the past month, it signals a broad-based contraction in the housing sector that reduces consumer spending and economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 1% in last month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST and RSAFS both decline >1%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market tightening regime (defined by UNRATE < 4.0 and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% per month), a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals an unexpected labor market deterioration that increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% per month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0 and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% per month and UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
